# Golden vectors

These files are the contract.

`golden/*.json` are trace inputs. `golden/*.bin` are the bytes this codec must
produce from them. Both are committed, and both are read by the test suite of
this module — and, more to the point, by the test suites of the two programs
that are built against it. The capture client and the server live in separate
repositories and are written by people who cannot see each other's code. What
keeps them interoperable is not a document; it is these files, which each side
asserts against independently.

A consumer locates them with:

    go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/pacenote-sim/protocol

and reads `trace/testdata/golden` beneath it.

## What is covered, and why each one is there

| Vector | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `empty` | A lap with no samples still produces a blob a decoder accepts |
| `single` | One point: every stream is one delta against zero and nothing else |
| `lap-300` | The shape every budget in `docs/SERVER.md` is quoted against |
| `lap-4096-cap` | Exactly `MaxPoints`, the largest trace that is legal at all |
| `no-gps` | `la` and `lo` both zero is *absent*, not invalid |
| `extremes` | Every channel on both ends of its range, alternating: the worst case for delta coding |
| `constant-run` | A stationary car, so eleven streams are a long run of zeroes |

`fuzz/FuzzDecode/` is the committed seed corpus: each golden blob, plus
truncations and single-byte corruptions of each. `go test` runs a seed corpus as
ordinary test cases, so a finding stays failing after the fuzzer that found it
has stopped.

## Regenerating them

    go test ./trace -update

**Do not do this to make a failing test pass.** The test failing is the format
telling you it changed. Two cases, and they are not the same case:

**The meaning changed.** A channel was added, a range widened, the stream order
moved, the delta scheme altered. Old blobs in a database will no longer decode
correctly, so this needs `CodecVersion` bumped in `trace/codec.go`, a decoder
kept for the old version, and the client and the server both updated. The golden
vectors are regenerated as the *last* step, and the diff is reviewed byte for
byte.

**Only the representation changed.** A `klauspost/compress` upgrade compresses
the same plaintext into different bytes. Nothing about the format changed and no
version bump is needed — but before regenerating, confirm that every committed
`.bin` still decodes to its committed `.json` under the new library, because that
is the direction that matters: old blobs are already written and will be read
back for years.

The encoder settings the `.bin` files were produced with are in `trace/codec.go`:
zstd `SpeedDefault`, CRC on, a 512 KiB window. Changing any of them changes every
`.bin` file, and falls under the second case above.

`.json` inputs are generated by the deterministic functions in
`trace/vectors_test.go`, so the whole tree is reproducible from source. Changing
one of those generators changes an input, which changes the bytes, which is the
first case above whether or not it was meant to be.
